audit.whatIsWrong: Row 0 read 'Skill' and row 6 read 'Skill' in both layers; the packet chart gives Volibear and Zac. The whys already said 'Level 1-2 is yours' and 'Late game Zac out-scales', so both rows printed a token against their own sentence.
audit.why: Level 1 is a clean Volibear win — his stat block against a Zac who leaks health with every Stretching Strikes cast and has to walk onto the blob to get it back. Late, Cell Division's revive and blob sustain plus Let's Bounce! (120/105/90s) make him a teamfight tank you cannot solo, which content late already states.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 6 set to Volibear and Zac in both layers as one atomic group, ratings moved to 6/10 and 3/10, and both whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why claimed Volibear is a drain-tank Zac cannot burst at two items — the stage the packet gives to Zac.
audit.why: Zac's late-game threat was never burst. Cell Division sheds a reabsorbable chunk on every ability hit and revives him from bloblets on fatal damage, and Unstable Matter deals a percentage of maximum health, so tank items make him harder to kill AND better at killing a health-stacking bruiser. 'He can't burst you' misreads the threat completely.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why now names the blob resets and Let's Bounce! and redirects you to grouping and locking his carries.

audit.whatIsWrong: Volibear's Q is called a slow in three fields — whys[0], spikes[0].text and content.early.
audit.why: Thundering Smash (Q, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, 300 range) grants speed toward enemies and stuns the first one he attacks; the slows in his kit are Sky Splitter (E, 16s) and Stormbringer (R). Against Zac the stun is what matters — it is the thing that stops him mid-step and prevents the blob pickup, which a slow would not.
audit.corrected: All three now say the Q stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid told you to walk him down 'whenever his E slingshot is unavailable' without ever saying how long that window lasts.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s. Through the levels this line covers it is an 18-15s gap, which is long enough to commit a full pattern and reset — and by late it is 9s, when the same advice stops being true. The number is what makes it actionable.
audit.corrected: content.mid now carries the 18s rank-2 figure and states he cannot disengage twice inside it.

audit.why: The _missing-interactions rule 'Elastic Slingshot shuts off Stormbringer' fires off a grounding flag on Zac's E, but Riot's own description of that ability is only 'attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward' — no grounding effect is described. Per the run's rule the description wins over a suspect derived flag, and the mirror audit declined to assert it too. Nothing about grounding Stormbringer was added to this page.

edits.after: W start for the bite-trade: your stat block and the Q stun beat blob poke, and he leaks health every time he steps up to throw it.

edits.before: With two items you're a drain-tank Zac can't burst. Only discipline beats you now — never int the Q stun into ready CC and the lane stays yours.
edits.after: Two items in he out-scales you as a tank: blob resets and Let's Bounce! peel your dives, so group and lock down his carries instead.

edits.before: Level 1-2 is yours as your stat block and Q slow out-trade Zac's blob poke.
edits.after: Level 1-2 is yours as your stat block and the Q stun out-trade Zac's blob poke.

edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay firmly in your favour as your full Q-W-E combo out-DPS his kit and Elastic Slingshot is 18s at rank 2, so he cannot disengage twice. Walk him down inside that window and force trades before his tank items land.

notes: Rows 0 and 6 realigned to the packet in both layers, and three 'Q slow' references corrected — Thundering Smash stuns, Sky Splitter and Stormbringer are the slows. I deliberately did NOT add the _missing-interactions claim that Elastic Slingshot grounds and denies Stormbringer: it fires off a grounding flag, but Riot's text for that ability describes only a self-launch, and the mirror audit reached the same conclusion. Also left alone: whether standing on a blob denies the pickup outright or merely contests it is not in Riot's text, so the existing 'deny blobs by standing on them' wording was not strengthened.
